issues.title_en: Acute-phase clinical profile and quality of life in patients with chikungunya during the 2025 outbreak in Bangladesh: A facility-based cross-sectional study
issues.summary: Author summary In 2025, Bangladesh experienced a renewed outbreak of chikungunya after its last major epidemic in 2017. We assessed 442 adults with laboratory-confirmed chikungunya to describe their clinical features and the impact of the illness on daily functioning and well-being. Nearly all patients reported fever and joint pain, and more than half experienced severe pain. A large proportion of participants reported difficulties with walking, self-care, usual activities, or emotional well-being, indicating a substantial burden of illness. Although most patients were managed as outpatients, approximately one in six required hospital admission. Overall perceived health and quality of life were markedly reduced during the acute phase of infection. Women and individuals with more intense pain experienced disproportionately greater impairment. These findings highlight the considerable individual and health system burden of chikungunya during outbreaks and underscore the need for effective clinical management and supportive care strategies in endemic settings.
